strengths: Hook to question reads as one clean thought: said it once, say it again, quiet and steady gets through, what's worth repeating.
Drop at 15.16s lands exactly on the question-to-screen-1 cut, and the energy climb through the screens (3 to 6 to 7) matches the whip-cut pace.

Screen 3 (YOUR DAY, READ) is the strongest showcase beat: it shows the actual hexagram-becoming-hexagram reading with 'Study line 1 · day 1 of 6', which is specific and legible, not generic app chrome.
End card holds long enough (5.7 s) with a clean snap transition and the credit is fully readable for nearly 2 s.

changes.change: Replace the plate behind SCREEN 2 (THE BOOK OF CHANGES) with a different image; it currently reuses the same bonsai-mountain art as SCREEN 1, so two of the four screens look identical and the showcase reads as one screen twice.
changes.why: Visual repetition across half the showcase makes the app look like it has fewer distinct views than it does, weakening the showcase criterion.

changes.change: Give the hook a plate or moving background behind 'Said it once, nothing changed?' instead of plain white text on black.
changes.why: The line is relatable and legible, but a bare text card is the flattest visual in the short and does the least to stop a scroll compared to the hexagram build and plates that follow.

changes.change: On SCREEN 1, hold past the title-reveal animation frame (the still at 16.74s catches 'READ THE STRUC' mid-type) or start the screen's on-screen window a few frames later so the full title is visible for more of its 3.16 s.
changes.why: A viewer landing on that exact moment via scrub or a slow phone would see clipped-looking text even though it resolves quickly.

review.notes: Can't hear the track, so can't confirm the whip/zoom cut style actually feels tight against a 95 bpm building synth-pop track rather than just landing on the beat grid; worth a sound-on pass to check the 1-beat shake on the drop doesn't feel abrupt against the retro-pop character of the track.
